# Numbered Stages in Directory Names

Order is encoded in **filenames and directory names**, not in a table of contents. Present in seven
repositories. What varies — and it is the interesting part — is whether the number means *run this
first* or *read this first*.

## Numbering as run order

`Oracle-Database-Laboratories` and `Data-Warehousing-and-Business-Intelligence` both number
executables, and the number is a dependency edge:

- `sql/01_schema/` → `02_queries/` → `03_plsql/` → `04_object_relational/`, and inside each,
  `01_drop_all.sql` → `02_create_tables.sql` → `03_seed_data.sql`
- `sql/01_analytics/`, `sql/02_star_schema/{01_create,02_load}`, `project/twtr/sql/{01_staging,
  02_star_schema, 03_technical_indicators}`

You cannot load before you create — see [[etl-load-order]] — so the digits are load-bearing. The
`Data-Warehousing` README makes it explicit: "The mart must be created before it is loaded."

## Numbering as chapters

`Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories` (`lab1_Max_Cut` … `lab6_Neo4j`),
`Python-Programming-Laboratories` (`01_first_steps` … `13_sqlite_and_gui`),
`Cybersecurity-Engineering-Laboratories` (`01-02_classical_ciphers_and_entropy` …
`14_web_security_injection`) and `Information-Systems-Modelling` (`lab1/` … `lab7/`) use the number as
a reading order, with each directory carrying its own README and the root README walking them in
sequence.

`Information-Systems-Modelling` states the chapter metaphor outright — "each lab picks up exactly
where the last one left off" — and it is literally true: lab 3 is lab 2 plus authentication, lab 4 is
lab 3 plus AOP and uploads. See [[forward-copy-lab-progression]].

## Numbering as prose chapters

Only `Farley` puts the numbers on documents in a `docs/` directory: `01-architecture.md`,
`02-roadmap.md`, `03-android-permissions-and-legal.md`, `04-accessibility-service.md`, plus a
newest-first `CHANGELOG.md` and a README index table mapping each chapter to what it covers. See
[[numbered-docs-chapters]].

## Where the numbering moved inside the files

Several repos have the instinct without the filenames. `Optimization Methods` numbers chapters 01–24
inside `chapters.js`, sections §1–§10 inside `ARCHITECTURE.md`, figures `fig1`–`fig11`, and operator
combinations `C01`–`C32` — but its `docs/` filenames are unnumbered SHOUTY topics.
`Information-Systems-Modelling/lab7` numbers its BPMN processes `p1-backup.bpmn` … `p8-eol.bpmn` with
matching SVGs and `specs.js` constants. `labour-fraud-analysis` numbers only its notebook and its
prose headings.

## Why it works here

These repos are read by someone arriving cold, which is the same premise as
[[readme-as-guided-tour]]. A sorted directory listing is a table of contents that cannot drift out of
sync with itself — a useful property in a source set where prose does drift, per
[[documentation-drift]]. The numbering survives even when the README describing it goes stale.
